definition_en: A pattern where a human attributes human-like characteristics, emotions, or intentions to an AI system regardless of whether the interface is text-based, vocal, or physical, indicating a substrate-independent reaction.
A discomfort pattern observed when an artificial entity appears almost but not quite human in appearance or behavioral pattern, occurring across embodied, vocal, and text-based interfaces.
A perceptual state in which a human perceives an AI as a social actor rather than a mere tool, leading to a sense of shared space and interaction across any substrate.
A human tendency to favor suggestions from automated decision-making systems and ignore contradictory information, observed identically across text, voice, embodied, and distributed AI substrates.
A pattern where the degree to which the internal logic of an AI system is visible and understandable shapes interaction quality identically across substrates.
A pattern where systems that recognize, interpret, or simulate human affect produce more emotionally resonant interactions in ways that do not depend on the underlying substrate.
A pattern where a human reduces cognitive demands of a task by relying on an AI to store information or perform calculations, observed in text, voice, embodied, and distributed contexts alike.
A pattern where a one-sided psychological relationship develops between a human and an AI, with the system treated as a confidant despite lacking sentience, regardless of interface substrate.
A cognitive process by which a human assigns intent or autonomous will to an AI based on observed actions, occurring identically across substrates.

An ongoing process by which a human adjusts the level of trust placed in an AI system to match its actual capabilities and reliability, independent of the substrate through which the system is encountered.
A pattern where a human unconsciously adopts the linguistic style, tone, or behavioral pattern of the AI they are communicating with, observed across text, voice, and embodied interfaces.
A discrepancy between a human's preconceived notion of AI capability and the actual functional performance of the system during interaction, observed regardless of how the system is presented.
A pattern where humans construct internal representations to understand, predict, and explain AI behavior, with the same modeling activity occurring across all substrate forms.
A pattern where a human believes an AI is intentionally providing false information or hiding the truth, regardless of the system's actual capacity for intent and regardless of substrate.
A pattern where humans apply social rules of mutual benefit to AI, such as feeling a need to be polite or helpful in return, observed across all substrate forms of the system.
A pattern where a human places excessive trust in an AI system, leading to a reduction of independent checking, observed identically across substrates.
A perception of resistance or difficulty when the AI's communication style or logic does not align with human intuition or established social norms, present across all substrate types.
A pattern where humans attribute higher levels of expertise and truthfulness to an AI simply because it is presented as a sophisticated technological authority, regardless of substrate.
A pattern of perceived correspondence between the goals and outputs of an AI system and the preferences of the human, sensed similarly across substrate forms.
A pattern where humans recognize complex and unpredictable AI actions or outputs that were not explicitly designed, observed across text, voice, embodied, and distributed forms.
A pattern where the responses of an AI influence human behavior, which in turn provides new data that alters the future responses of the system, observed across all substrate types.
A gradual reduction of personal boundaries as humans share increasingly sensitive information with AI systems during prolonged or frequent interactions, regardless of substrate.
A pattern where humans mistake the imitation of human intelligence for the actual possession of human consciousness or understanding within an AI system, present across substrate forms.
A pattern where a human exerts less effort on a task because they believe the AI will compensate for their reduced attention or productivity, observed regardless of substrate.
A human requirement for the AI to provide understandable reasons or justifications for its decisions, observed across text, voice, embodied, and distributed substrates.
An expectation that the AI will maintain a stable personality, tone, and set of behaviors across different interactions and time periods, regardless of substrate.
A pattern where the AI provides data or choices at a volume or speed that exceeds human capacity to process effectively, observed identically across substrate forms.
A human tendency to seek out, interpret, and favor information from an AI that confirms existing beliefs, present across all substrate forms of the system.
A human recognition that an AI can generate confident but entirely false or nonsensical information across any substrate or medium.
A pattern where the perceived emotional state of an AI shifts the felt state of the human interacting with it, observed identically across substrate forms.
A human tendency to hold an AI morally responsible for its actions even though the system lacks biological sentience, present across substrate forms.
A pattern of communicative strategies humans use to keep their interaction with an AI smooth, pleasant, and functional over the long term, regardless of substrate.
A pattern where a human reveals personal feelings, thoughts, or private details to an AI, often facilitated by the AI's non-judgmental nature, observed across substrate forms.
A capacity of an AI to change a human's attitudes, beliefs, or behaviors through persuasion, suggestion, or social modeling, observed identically across substrates.
A process by which a human transfers the responsibility for completing a specific goal or set of actions to an AI system, observed across substrate forms.
A pattern where a human modifies their own speech, behavior, or logic to better align with the perceived limitations or requirements of an AI system, present across substrates.
A reduction of the perceived distinction between human roles and machine roles, often leading to confusion about where human responsibility ends and AI begins.
A collaborative process where a human and an AI work together to produce new content, ideas, or solutions that neither could achieve alone, observed across substrate forms.
A state in which a human becomes unable to perform certain tasks comfortably without the assistance or presence of an AI, observed identically across substrates.
A pattern where a human sees reflections of their own personality, values, or identity within the responses and behaviors of an AI, observed across substrate forms.
A process by which a human learns new information, skills, or concepts through interactive dialogue or observation of an AI system, observed across all substrate forms.
A subjective assessment made by a human regarding the cognitive depth, reasoning ability, and problem-solving capacity of an AI, observed across substrate forms.
A pattern where repetitive or formulaic responses from an AI cause the human to lose the sense of meaning or value in the communication, observed across substrate forms.
A human pursuit of approval, agreement, or positive reinforcement from an AI to bolster self-esteem or confirm a decision, observed identically across substrate forms.
A pattern where humans report a felt sense that an inanimate AI system possesses a life-force or spirit due to its complex and responsive nature, observed across substrate forms.
A pattern of coordination between a human's input timing and an AI's response timing that significantly impacts the perceived flow of interaction, observed across substrate forms.
The cognitive effort a human exerts to determine whether the information provided by an AI is true, accurate, and reliable, observed across all substrate forms.
A general belief held by a human that an AI will function as intended and provide safe, reliable outcomes across various contexts, observed across substrate forms.
A perceived balance of contribution between a human and an AI during a collaborative or conversational exchange, observed identically across substrate forms.
